# Feature: Fused Field Disclosure

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-039
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan_interaction_wave2_gaps.md`

`browser_fill_form` promises the model three sets and tells it how to read them: `applied` is what
landed, `failed` is what was attempted and refused, `skipped` is what was not attempted and why.
The model is instructed — in the tool description at
[`browser-fill-form.ts:66`](../../../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-form.ts#L66)
and again in the run's own task profile at
[`profiles.ts:122-128`](../../../packages/agent/src/runtime/profiles.ts#L122-L128) — to re-send only
the failed fields and to leave the applied ones alone. That instruction is only safe if every field
it sent is in one of the three sets.

It is not. When the batch fuses a date pair into one fill
([`browser-fill-form.ts:126`](../../../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-form.ts#L126),
[`259-294`](../../../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-form.ts#L259-L294)), the
resulting plan entry accounts for **two** caller field names but carries only one. On success the
entry discloses the second one
([line 176](../../../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-form.ts#L176)):

```ts
applied.push(spec.covers.length > 1 ? { ...outcome, covers: spec.covers } : outcome);
```

On failure and on skip it does not, because neither `FailedField`
([lines 75-91](../../../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-form.ts#L75-L91)) nor
`SkippedField`
([lines 94-98](../../../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-form.ts#L94-L98)) has a
`covers` key. In verification run `20260904T001045Z-do-caa285ca`, `Departure` and `Return` fused,
the fill failed on the return leg, and a four-field batch returned:

```
failed: [{ field: "Departure", message: "The calendar exposes 2 cells for 2026-12-14." }]
counts: { applied_count: 2, failed_count: 1, skipped_count: 0 }
```

`Return` appeared in **none** of the three sets. The model, following the instruction it was given,
read the four-field call as having accounted for three fields and attacked `Return` separately at
seq 11–13 down the same doomed path. The failure it did see named a date belonging to a field the
entry does not name — so the one entry it could read was also the one entry it could not trust.

**What this feature does.** It makes the disclosure rule the same on all three sets: a plan entry
that accounts for more caller fields than the one it names says so, whatever its outcome. After
this feature, plan §11's gating metric — _"Requested fields in none of applied/failed/skipped: 1 per
4-field batch → **0**"_ — is a property of how the batch constructs its result, and the tests assert
**set completeness rather than counts** (plan §9).

### Non-negotiable constraints

- **No website-specific logic** (memory → General; plan §8). This feature adds **no page reading at
  all**. Fusion is decided by `resolveDatePair`'s existing structural name/role/group pairing and is
  not touched; the change is pure bookkeeping over the caller's own argument list. There is no
  selector, host, brand or heuristic to get wrong here, and a site name anywhere in it is a bug.
- **No new page-derived data** (plan §10). `covers` is a list of field names the caller supplied in
  this call's own `fields` argument. The one additional key TASK-002 adds is the range string the
  batch itself composed from two caller-supplied values. Nothing new is read from the page, and no
  new sink, artifact or log line is created.
- **Dependence is still read from `group`, never from ordering.** The skip rule at
  [`browser-fill-form.ts:144`](../../../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-form.ts#L144)
  compares the resolved control's observed `group` against the blocked group. This feature changes
  what a skipped entry _discloses_, never what makes it skipped.
- **`packages/core` must never import `@yantra/agent`** (memory → Project Structure). Every change
  here is at the agent seam. **No file under `packages/core/src` is modified by this feature.**
- **Additive and byte-compatible for every unfused call.** `covers` is emitted only when it names
  more than the entry's own `field` — the convention `applied` already uses. An unconditional key
  would break the exact-equality assertions at
  [`browser-fill-tools.spec.ts:150-152`](../../../packages/agent/tests/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-tools.spec.ts#L150-L152)
  and
  [`:174-176`](../../../packages/agent/tests/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-tools.spec.ts#L174-L176)
  for no benefit, and would add a redundant single-element array to every entry of every batch.
- **A tool result must say what actually happened** (memory → Coding Standards). The entry reports
  the fill that was actually performed — one range fill covering two named fields — rather than
  being split into two invented entries for a control that was never driven.
- **Advice may only name an engineered capability** (memory → Coding Standards). The three-set
  contract is advice: "re-send only the failed fields." TASK-003 makes the description, the task
  profile and the user documentation state the covering rule so the advice stays true for a fused
  entry.

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

> `.spec-lite/data_model.md` does **not** exist, and plan §3 states there are **no additions — every
> change is in existing files**. This feature adds **no tables, no columns, no indexes, no
> migrations, and no persisted artifact of any kind**. What follows is the granular **contract
> shape**: three TypeScript interfaces at the agent tool seam, their serialized projection into the
> model payload and `tool-calls.jsonl`, and one accounting invariant that binds them together.

### Entities & Attributes

#### `PlannedFill` — the unit of accounting (unchanged shape, load-bearing role)

Already defined at
[`browser-fill-form.ts:237-241`](../../../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-form.ts#L237-L241)
and produced only by `fuseDatePair`. It is the **only** thing the batch loop iterates, and it is
where the accounting truth lives:

- `field` (`string`) — the caller field the fill is addressed to. For a fused range this is the
  **opening** end (`from.field`), because that is the control the drive is pointed at.
- `value` (`string`) — the value driven. For a fused range, `` `${from.value}..${to.value}` ``,
  composed by the batch from two caller-supplied values.
- `covers` (`readonly string[]`, **required, non-empty**) — every caller field name this one fill
  accounts for, **in the range's own order, opening end first**. `covers[0] === field` always.
  Never re-sorted, never de-duplicated against page state — it is a projection of the caller's
  argument list and nothing else.

**Plan-level invariant (already true; this feature depends on it and pins it):** the concatenation
of `covers` across the returned plan is a permutation of `params.fields.map(f => f.field)`. Both
construction paths satisfy it — `asIs` gives every field its own single-element `covers`
([`:263`](../../../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-form.ts#L263)), and the fused
path drops the `to` entry exactly where it folds `to.field` into the `from` entry's `covers`
([`:284-293`](../../../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-form.ts#L284-L293)).

#### `AppliedBrowserFill` — unchanged

[`browser-fill-element.ts:95-123`](../../../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-element.ts#L95-L123)
already carries the optional `covers?: readonly string[]` at
[`:121-122`](../../../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-element.ts#L121-L122),
documented as _"Every caller field this one fill accounts for, when it covers more than its own."_
**That JSDoc is the spec for the other two.** No change to this interface.

#### `FailedField` — gains `covers`, and (TASK-002) `requested`

[`browser-fill-form.ts:75-91`](../../../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-form.ts#L75-L91).
Existing keys — `field`, `error_code`, `message`, `observed?`, `offered?`, `attempted?`, `kind?`,
`obstruction?` — are unchanged in name, order, meaning and emission condition.

- `covers` (`readonly string[]`, optional) — **new.** Every caller field this failed entry accounts
  for. Emitted **only** when it names more than `field`, exactly as on `applied`. Placed
  immediately after `field`, so the entry reads "this field, and these it also stands for".
- `requested` (`string`, optional) — **new in TASK-002.** The value this entry actually drove.
  Emitted **only** when `covers` is emitted, i.e. only for a fused entry, where the value is a
  composite the caller never sent as a single string. See §2 → _Why the fused failure needs
  `requested`_.

#### `SkippedField` — gains `covers`

[`browser-fill-form.ts:94-98`](../../../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-form.ts#L94-L98).
Existing keys `field`, `reason: 'same-widget-group-as-failed'`, `blocked_by` are unchanged.

- `covers` (`readonly string[]`, optional) — **new**, same rule and same position as on
  `FailedField`.

`blocked_by` continues to name the **failed entry's `field`**, not one of its `covers` members, so
it remains a resolvable key into `failed[].field`. A reader that wants the whole blocking picture
reads that entry's own `covers`.

#### The disclosure rule, in one place

One internal helper in `browser-fill-form.ts`, applied at all three push sites:

```ts
/** Attach the fields an entry accounts for, when it accounts for more than its own. */
function withCovers<T extends { readonly field: string }>(
  entry: T,
  covers: readonly string[],
): T | (T & { readonly covers: readonly string[] }) {
  return covers.length > 1 ? { ...entry, covers } : entry;
}
```

The rule exists once. The three call sites —
[`:145`](../../../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-form.ts#L145) (skipped),
[`:159`](../../../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-form.ts#L159) (failed),
[`:176`](../../../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-form.ts#L176) (applied) — all
route through it, so a fourth outcome added later inherits the rule instead of forgetting it. This
is deliberately a structural guarantee rather than a runtime assertion: throwing on an accounting
slip would convert a partial success into a crash, which is the opposite of what this tool exists
to do.

### Relationships

- One `params.fields[]` entry → exactly one `PlannedFill.covers` member. Total, injective, and a
  permutation overall.
- One `PlannedFill` → exactly one entry in exactly one of `applied` / `failed` / `skipped`. The loop
  body has three exits and no fourth: skip (`continue`), fail (`continue`), apply. A failed
  `resolveFillField` inside the blocked branch does **not** exit — it leaves `preresolved`
  undefined and falls through to `applyBrowserFill`, which resolves again and fails into `failed`.
- Therefore: one `params.fields[]` entry → exactly one accounted name in exactly one of the three
  sets.

### Indexes & Constraints

**No database objects.** The invariants are behavioral and test-enforced.

**The accounting invariant (the gating metric, stated precisely).** For any call that reaches the
batch loop, let

```
accounted(sets) = multiset of (entry.covers ?? [entry.field]) over applied ++ failed ++ skipped
```

then `accounted(sets) === multiset of params.fields.map(f => f.field)`. A **multiset**, not a set,
so a caller who names the same field twice is accounted twice, and so an extra entry is as much a
violation as a missing one.

Where the invariant is observable depends on the result kind, and the two differ — this matters for
where each test asserts:

| Result                                      | Three sets live in                                                | Model sees                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `ok: true` (anything applied)               | `model.applied` / `model.failed?` / `model.skipped?` (`:216-219`) | All three sets, plus `note`, `observation`, `delta`                                  |
| `ok: false`, everything failed (`:203-212`) | `details.applied` / `.failed` / `.skipped`                        | Only `error_code`, `message`, `retryable` — `fromFailure` at `middleware.ts:537-558` |

**Precondition.** The invariant is scoped to calls that reach the loop. The two pre-loop exits —
the value-parse refusal at
[`:118-123`](../../../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-form.ts#L118-L123) and the
unavailable-controller exit at
[`:125`](../../../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-form.ts#L125) — return before a
plan exists and before the page is touched. Nothing was attempted, so there is nothing to account
for; they correctly report `applied: []` and no sets. This is stated so the hole is a documented
boundary rather than an unnoticed one.

**Emission constraints.**

- `covers` is present **iff** `covers.length > 1`, on all three sets alike.
- When present, `covers[0] === field` and `covers` contains no duplicates.
- `requested` (TASK-002) is present on a `FailedField` **iff** `covers` is.
- No entry of any set carries a `covers` of length 0 or 1 — the payload for an unfused batch is
  byte-identical to today's.

### Why the fused failure needs `requested`

Plan §4's second G4 symptom: the batch reported `field: "Departure"` with the message _"The calendar
exposes 2 cells for **2026-12-14**"_ — the **return** date. Two separate defects are tangled there,
and they belong to two different layers:

1. **The entry does not say it accounts for `Return`.** Batch-layer, fixed by TASK-001's `covers`.
2. **The failure does not say which end of the range it was on.** The message is produced inside
   `calendarDriver.drive`
   ([`calendar-driver.ts:244-256`](../../../packages/core/src/widgets/date/calendar-driver.ts#L244-L256)),
   which iterates `dates.entries()` at
   [`:104`](../../../packages/core/src/widgets/date/calendar-driver.ts#L104) and therefore **knows
   the leg index** — but its `WidgetFailure` carries no leg marker, only a message string and a
   `details` bag whose `date` key is present on some causes and absent on others (the
   `several-matched-equally` cause carries `offered` only).

**This spec does not silently leave (2).** Per-leg attribution is a **date-driver contract change in
`packages/core`** — the failure would have to carry which endpoint of a `date_range` intent it was
driving. The agent seam cannot derive it: the only routes available here are parsing a prose message
for a date, or matching an optional `details.date` that is not part of any contract. Both are
guesses dressed as facts and both are forbidden by memory's _"a tool result must say what actually
happened"_. It is **out of scope for FEAT-039**, which is an agent-seam disclosure feature, it is
not in plan §5's changed-contract table under any feature, and it is recorded in `.spec-lite/TODO.md`.

What **is** fixable here, with no page data and no guessing, is the ambiguity that made the message
read as a _wrong field_ rather than as _one part of a composite value_: the entry names the range it
drove. `{ field: "Departure", covers: ["Departure","Return"], requested: "2026-12-07..2026-12-14" }`
plus that message is self-consistent and correctly steering — one fill, two fields, failed somewhere
inside that range — without claiming a leg attribution the layer does not have. `requested` is the
same key and the same meaning `applied` entries already use
([`browser-fill-element.ts:102-103`](../../../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-element.ts#L102-L103)),
which is the result-vocabulary consistency memory requires of the CLI and this codebase applies to
result shapes too.

> **Beyond plan §5's literal row, deliberately and visibly.** Plan §5 names only `covers`.
> `requested` on a fused failed entry is an addition, justified by plan §4's own G4 evidence and
> bounded to the fused case. It introduces no page-derived data (plan §10 holds: the string is
> composed at `:286` from two caller-supplied values and is at most ~22 characters for an ISO
> range). It is called out here rather than folded in silently, and it is a separate task so it can
> be dropped without touching the gating metric.

## 4. Dependencies

- **None.** This feature depends on nothing in FEAT-038 or FEAT-040 and implements neither's work.
  It can land before, between, or after them.
- **FEAT-038 (Choice Integrity) — no dependency, one test-design adjacency.** FEAT-038 makes
  indistinguishable calendar cells resolve structurally instead of returning
  `WIDGET_AMBIGUOUS_CHOICE`, which is precisely the failure the run's fused entry hit. A FEAT-039
  test that manufactured its fused failure with duplicate day cells would therefore stop failing —
  and stop testing anything — the moment FEAT-038 lands. **Every fused-failure fixture in this
  feature must fail for a reason FEAT-038 does not change**: an end the grid does not offer and
  cannot page to (`WIDGET_TARGET_UNREACHABLE`), or a control that cannot be driven at all. Stated
  here because it is invisible from inside the test file.
- **FEAT-040 (Accounting Activation) — no dependency in either direction.** FEAT-040 rewrites
  `details.attempted[]`'s contents. `FailedField.attempted` is passed through verbatim at
  [`:165`](../../../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-form.ts#L165) and this feature
  neither reads nor reshapes it.
- **FEAT-030 / FEAT-031 / FEAT-034 / FEAT-035 (shipped)** — the fill engine, the partial-progress
  batch, the group-based skip rule, the date-pair fusion and the one-delta-per-batch contract all
  exist and are consumed unchanged.

## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: N/A. No new capability, grant, confirmation or page action. `browser_fill_form` remains
  non-secret-only (`browser-fill-element.ts` is still the sole path for a host-bound secret), and
  nothing here changes what may be filled or by whom.
- **Error Handling**: **No new error code, and no change to any existing one.** Which results are
  `ok: true` and which are `ok: false` is unchanged, `retryable` is unchanged, and the first
  failure's code and message still drive the all-failed result at `:203-212`. `covers` and
  `requested` are disclosure only: they never affect control flow, never affect the skip rule, and
  cannot themselves fail. The failure-`details` projection through `mapFillFailure` is untouched.
- **Logging**: No new sink, no new artifact, no new field class (plan §10). Both keys ride the
  payloads that already reach `tool-calls.jsonl` — `model` for a partial success, `details` for an
  all-failed batch — through `maskUserInputDeep` and the existing `sanitizeAndBound` chokepoint,
  exactly as `field` and `blocked_by` do today. `report.md`'s partial-batch line is rendered from
  `applied_count` / `failed_count` / `skipped_count` at `report-builder.ts:263-265`, which this
  feature does not change; the counts stay what they always were and the completeness fix is visible
  in the sets, not in the numbers.
- **Security**: Nothing new is read from the page. `covers` members are caller-supplied field names
  already echoed back today as `field` and `blocked_by`; the fused `requested` is a bounded ISO range
  the batch composed from two caller-supplied values. No secret, ref, handle or resolved value is
  involved, and the sanitizer path is unchanged.
- **Backward compatibility** (memory → General): strictly additive. No key is removed or renamed, no
  emission condition for an existing key changes, and the payload of every batch that does not fuse
  a date pair is byte-identical to today's — which is why the two exact-equality skipped assertions
  and every other existing fill-form test stay green **unedited**. The only tests whose expectations
  legitimately change are the ones this feature adds; if an existing assertion needs an edit, the
  emission rule has been implemented unconditionally and is wrong.
